clues: This city in Iran lies south of Tehran, the nation's capital, on the banks of a river. Tehran is the big city to its north, a long drive away.
This city sits far from the sea, so rain stays low all year long. Summers are hot and dry, yet cold air from Siberia can plunge in in winter.
In 1956, oil was found in fields near this city. A big refinery was built soon after, on the road north to Tehran.
This city is the world's top hub for Shia study and learning. Near twenty million pilgrims visit its shrines and schools each year.
The shrine of Fatima Masumeh is the heart of this holy city. It is a famed site of the Shia faith, known far and wide.
